Exploding Kittens is a kitty-powered version of Russian Roulette. Players take turns drawing cards until someone draws an exploding kitten and loses the game. The deck is made up of cards that let you avoid exploding by peeking at cards before you draw, forcing your opponent to draw multiple cards, or shuffling the deck. The game gets more and more intense with each card you draw because fewer cards left in the deck means a greater chance of drawing the kitten and exploding in a fiery ball of feline hyperbole. These latest rules for example do not include the 5 card combo. Contents 1 Overview 2 Turn 2.1 Special Combos 3 Cards Overview Be the last player left after all others are eliminated. Turn On your turn, you can play no cards or as many as you wish. Then, draw 1 card. If this is an Exploding Kitten and you cannot counter it in any way, you are out! Special Combos If you Play two cards of the same name, you can take a random card from someone else. If you Play three cards of the same name, you can ask for a particular card, but get nothing if that player does not have it. Cards This BGA Adaptation uses an optimized card distribution for online play. [Rating: 1/10] The game basically plays itself. You're there to hold the cards and play them when required.  No real strategy except deciding when to draw cards the rest is very obvious moves.  I can't really recommend this game for anyone unless they really like cats and bombs. The one good thing about the game is it can play relatively quickly since you don't really make any choices.  The art is funny for about the first couple of cards as it gets repetitive quite quickly.

[Rating: 1/10] Everything about this game is terrible. The art is oatmeal so I suppose that's decent. Never play this game.

[Rating: 1/10] Just because you have a successful comic does not mean you can design a board game. Sure it's funny, the first time and then never again. Sub-gateway trash with next to no meaningful decisions. Id rather play Munchkin or Monopoly. (not a good thing)

[Rating: 1/10] Rating based on 2 plays.  The player elimination element is very poorly done. Early elimination coupled with kittens on the bottom of the deck means that people were sitting around for 10+ minutes waiting for a new round. This is just poor design for a party game.  Gameplay/strategy is pretty brainless too. Draw like crazy while you have a defuse in your hand - do everything to avoid drawing when you don't.  This "game" seems to be popular merely because it is trying to be border-line offensive.   This is really just a bad game and is best avoided.

[Rating: 1/10] Fun/amusing art, little strategy and I was ready to be done with it after 20 minutes.

[Rating: 1/10] Insufferably awful.  The worst part about this game is that people actually think it isn't awful.

[Rating: 1/10] It has a lot of things I do not like. Pure take that, pure luck based, zero thought, almost completely random. Just make sense to draw the whole deck to start the game. Also it has player elimination. The art and humor is good but the game has no thought, there are much better fillers out there than this, even ones that take similar levels of thought.

[Rating: 1/10] Me: "Okay, 'good game'". Caitlin: "What?  But we're not done?" Me: "Yes we are."  Clyde: "Insufferably awful.  The worst part about this game is that people actually think it isn't awful."

[Rating: 1/10] Kickstarter. One game was enough. I really wanted to like this game, but it's just waster of time and money :(

[Rating: 1/10] Silly and pointless game, completely governed by luck of the draw. Decisions are minimal and obvious. The artwork is atrocious.

[Rating: 1/10] This... thing... is not a game. At best, it is an activity.
